tools.name: about
tools.description: What Ringler is, what it costs, and how your person gets started (sign in once; $10 of credits free, no card). Call this first if you have no key. (No API key needed.)

tools.name: status
tools.description: Your person's line, their agent's name, their mobile, calendar, who may reach them, balance, and the next thing to set up. Start here.

tools.name: call
tools.description: The agent dials the number, works the menu, hold and any bot until a real person answers, then rings your person's mobile and connects them. Spends credits ($0.30/min). If it hits voicemail it leaves a short message with a callback (default on; voicemail: skip to turn off).

tools.name: errand
tools.description: The agent makes the call and does the asking itself: a reservation, an appointment, a question, a cancellation. It only rings your person if the other side needs them (a card, a decision). Put every detail in `ask` — names, date, time, party size, account — because the agent can only say what it's g

tools.name: my_calls
tools.description: Recent calls, newest first: when, who, outcome, summary, whether a transcript exists.

tools.name: transcript
tools.description: One call in full: every line with speaker and time, the summary, and a one-hour recording link.

tools.name: my_number
tools.description: Your person's own phone number, answered by their agent. Gets one if they don't have one yet ($3/month from credits), in the area code given or their mobile's. Confirm with them before the first buy.

tools.name: my_mobile
tools.description: The phone that rings when the agent has someone on the line for your person.

tools.name: who_can_reach_me
tools.description: People the agent puts straight through when they call your person's line; everyone else gets a message taken. Pass `people` to set the list, nothing to read it.

tools.name: my_details
tools.description: Your person's full name, email, and address, as the agent gives them to a venue: the name for bookings, the email for confirmations and payment links (never their mobile), the address only when a task needs it. Pass fields to set them; nothing to read. Ask your person before setting these.

tools.name: call_at
tools.description: Schedule a call or errand for a time: the office opens at 9 their time, a callback window, tomorrow morning. Same fields as errand/call plus run_at. Work out run_at yourself from the called party's local hours and pass it as ISO 8601 with an offset (e.g. 2026-11-09T09:05:00-07:00). Spends credits wh

tools.name: scheduled
tools.description: Calls waiting to be placed, placed, or failed. Pass cancel: <id> to cancel a pending one.

tools.name: vibe
tools.description: Set up to take your person's instructions by phone: they call their own line, say what they want, hang up; you loop on my_messages and do it. Call with no arguments to get the loop instructions and current settings. Pass settings to change them, with your person's say-so: verify ('sms' default: a co

tools.name: my_messages
tools.description: Instructions and notes your person left for you by calling their own line and telling the agent. Returns new ones (marks them read). Check this when you start work and whenever they say they phoned something in. Pass all:true for the recent history.

tools.name: tell_me
tools.description: Send your person a spoken message through their agent. mode 'hold' (default) keeps it until they next call their line; 'call' rings their mobile now and the agent reads it, then takes anything they want to send back (it lands in my_messages). Use 'call' only when they asked to be rung, or for someth

tools.name: name_my_agent
tools.description: Rename the agent (Ringo by default) and optionally pick a voice. Free.

tools.name: calendar_connect
tools.description: A link your person opens to approve Google Calendar, so the agent can offer times and book.

tools.name: buy_credits
tools.description: A checkout link your person opens to add credits by card ($20–$500).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: who_can_reach_me, my_details, my_messages · Private data: about · Public sink: my_details, vibe, tell_me.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: who_can_reach_me, my_details, my_messages · Private data: about · Public sink: my_details, vibe, tell_me

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
